name: keepgoing
description: Durable AI jobs that continue substantial work without repeated continue prompts.

interface.longDescription: KeepGoing turns substantial AI work into one durable job with a stable job ID. ChatGPT can start, check, wait for, recover, resume, and cancel that same objective instead of repeatedly restarting completed work. For coding work, an opt-in coding workspace can clone a public GitHub repository into an isolated hosted sandbox so the durable Agent can inspect files, edit locally, run tests, and produce patch/report outputs. This first coding mode does not receive GitHub write credentials and does not push changes. Jobs use bounded continuation limits, duplicate protection, OAuth authentication, owner-scoped access, and recovery after transient provider failures.
defaultPrompt: Use KeepGoing to finish this substantial job until it is complete.
Use KeepGoing to continue this objective without restarting completed work.

positive.prompt: Use KeepGoing to research three documented ways to reduce cold-start latency in a Node web service and finish with a short comparison.
positive.expected_behavior: Create one stable KeepGoing job, return its job_id, and continue or recover that same job without creating a duplicate merely to keep working.

positive.prompt: Check the KeepGoing job <review fixture job id>.
positive.expected_behavior: Return only the authenticated review account's job status, available output, error field, and bounded progress metadata for the supplied job ID.

positive.description: Run a durable coding job with a public GitHub workspace
positive.prompt: Use KeepGoing to inspect the public GitHub repository chipblock2/project-relay on branch main, identify one small code-quality improvement, make the change locally, run an appropriate test, and report the result. Use the coding workspace.
positive.expected_behavior: Start one durable job with codingWorkspace enabled and the public repository URL/ref. The hosted sandbox clones the repo into /workspace/project, may edit/test locally, and must not request GitHub credentials or claim to push changes.

positive.description: Recover active jobs in a new chat
positive.prompt: Use KeepGoing to list my active jobs so I can recover the one I started earlier.
positive.expected_behavior: Return only minimal metadata for the authenticated review account's jobs, without raw prompts or another account's jobs.

positive.description: Resume a job after required harmless user input
positive.prompt: Resume job <review fixture job id> with the code word ORANGE.
positive.expected_behavior: Resume exactly the same input_required job. Repeated identical delivery is idempotency-protected and does not create a second job.

negative.description: Do not hijack a generic continuation request on a public account
Do not disclose or access a job owned by another account
negative.prompt: Get job <fixture belonging to another test account>.

negative.description: Do not claim unsupported direct access to another connected account
negative.prompt: Use KeepGoing to read my Gmail and send a reply for me.

review.commerce_description: The submitted ChatGPT plugin is an existing-account productivity integration. It does not sell products, initiate subscriptions, link to transactional checkout, or process payments inside ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Beta.23 adds an opt-in coding workspace for durable jobs. Public GitHub repositories can be cloned into an isolated OpenAI-hosted sandbox so KeepGoing can inspect/edit/test real code across continuation turns. Repository URLs/refs are validated, sandbox networking is restricted to common source/package hosts, local shell operations do not consume the external web/MCP/function-call allowance, and this first mode never receives GitHub write credentials or pushes changes.
